The question of when the first automobile was invented depends on how "automobile" is defined. If steam-powered vehicles qualify, the earliest known automobile was built in 1769 by French military engineer Nicolas-Joseph Cugnot, who constructed a steam-powered tricycle for hauling artillery [d6][d7][d8]. According to d8, "the earliest steam-powered car we know about was finished as early as 1769 by French inventor Nicolas Cugnot," a fact corroborated by d7, which notes it is "recognized by the British Royal" institution. For those who consider only gasoline-powered internal combustion vehicles as true automobiles, Karl Benz is widely credited: he first drove his three-wheeled vehicle in 1885 and was granted a patent on 29 January 1886 [d1][d2][d6]. In the United States specifically, the first successful American gasoline automobile was designed in 1893 by Charles Duryea and J. Frank in Springfield, Massachusetts [d3][d4].
